title: MaterialsManifest
description: course/materials/manifest.yaml — every material the course has ingested (D-035, spec §8.7). Written by `classkit ingest`; `kind`, `units`, `title` and `audience` are proposed by the classifying agent, recorded by `/ingest` through `classkit material apply` (D-039), and are the teacher's to correct. A material is never deleted from this list: a removed source is marked `removed_at`, a merged duplicate is marked `merged_into`, so an id is never reused and a locator pointing at either fails visibly.

id.description: Assigned once, never reused, e.g. 'M0007'. Locators cite it: 'M0007#slide-18'.

title.description: From the file's first heading, slide title or metadata; for a link, its fetched title or note. Editable — re-ingest keeps it.

format.description: File extension without the dot ('pptx', 'pdf', 'docx', 'md'), or 'url' for a link.

kind.description: Guessed from the format at ingest, then set by the classifying agent; correctable by the teacher.

sources.description: Paths relative to materials/source/, or the URL for a link. More than one when duplicates were merged.

canonical.description: Which of `sources` the anchors refer to — a PPTX over its PDF export, since 'slide 18' beats 'page 18'.

source_hash.description: Hash of the canonical source as it was when last converted ('sha256:…'). When it differs from source_hashes[canonical], the source changed and has not been re-ingested yet.

source_hashes.description: The current hash of every path in `sources`. How a renamed or moved file is re-matched to its id, including a merged duplicate that is not the canonical source.

ingested_hash.description: Hash of the .md file ingest last wrote. A different hash on disk means the teacher edited it, and re-ingest refuses to replace it without asking.

status.description: ingested: text extracted with anchors. unsupported: no extractor (see status_reason). no-text: a PDF with no text layer (needs OCR; pages are still anchored). media: audio or video, recorded but not extracted. link: a URL — the material is the link.

status_reason.description: Why a material was not extracted, and what to do, e.g. 'install LibreOffice, or export to PDF'.

units.description: Units this material appears to support — a hint set by the classifying agent.

found_in.description: For a link discovered inside another material: where it was found, e.g. 'M0007' or 'M0007#slide-3'.

note.description: For a link: the note written after it in links.md.

duration.description: For a video link: its length ('12:03', '1:02:45'), when the page declares it.

removed_at.description: Set when the source disappeared. The record and its ingested file are kept, so a locator to it fails validation visibly rather than vanishing.

merged_into.description: Set when the teacher confirmed this material is the same as another (a PDF export of a deck). Its sources moved to that material; this id is retired, never reused.

private.description: True when the canonical source is under materials/source/private/ (D-040), which is gitignored: the committed ingested file is then an index (its anchors and one-line labels, `text: index`) and the full text lives in the gitignored materials/private-text/. Set by ingest from the path as last converted, never by hand; recorded so a clone without the file still knows.

private_text_hash.description: RETIRED (D-041) — was the hash of a private material's full text in materials/private-text/. A committed field cannot describe a machine-local file (extraction differs across library versions); the full text now certifies itself with `body_hash` in its own front matter. Accepted here only so a manifest written before D-041 still validates; ingest drops it when it next converts the material.

audience.description: Who may be pointed at this material (D-040); absent means 'student'. An 'instructor' material (a solutions manual, a past exam) cited from a student-facing place raises the alert instructor_material_cited, and no exporter may bundle it. Proposed by the classifying agent, confirmed by the teacher. Independent of `private`: a published textbook is private but 'student'.
